column11: With frame first, proof finishes before input here. The donor puts proof last. The disabled checks cover distinct incomplete states.

column5: **Given** The viewer is paused with the first tab selected and the later tab present; five hidden creations are made before the page becomes visible, with discovery checks pending for the selected and later tabs. **When** The selected tab's discovery check settles before the later tab's check. **Then** The live browser view is visible while browser input remains disabled during discovery. Once ready, the first tab is selected, and the user can navigate to the entered URL before the later discovery check settles.
column6: **Given** The viewer is paused with the first tab selected and the later tab present; one hidden creation is made before the page becomes visible, with discovery checks pending for the selected and later tabs. **When** The selected tab's discovery check settles before the later tab's check. **Then** The live browser view is visible while browser input remains disabled during discovery. Once ready, the first tab is selected, and the user can navigate to the entered URL before the later discovery check settles.
column11: Five queued creations exercise backlog pressure on selected-page resume. A single creation cannot establish progress through a multi-entry backlog.

column5: **Given** The viewer has recovered from a bad image; the target frame arrives before the capture-start receipt. **When** The primary window is maximized at 1280 by 720 and the user selects “Fit window to panel.” **Then** The window becomes normal, the viewport becomes 900 by 600, and input remains enabled.
column6: **Given** The viewer has recovered from a bad image; the capture-start receipt arrives before the target frame. **When** The primary window is maximized at 1280 by 720 and the user selects “Fit window to panel.” **Then** The window becomes normal, the viewport becomes 900 by 600, and input remains enabled.
column11: Frame-first and receipt-first image recovery hold different readiness prerequisites and test the input-disabled interval in opposite orders.

column5: **Given** The browser is connecting in the same-window mode, with its socket opening pending and one page in window 101. **When** The user switches to Separate image connection, then the pending socket is opened. **Then** The browser reaches an interactive state, retains the page at https://example.com, and still has exactly one target.
column6: **Given** The browser is connecting in the same-window mode, with native attachment pending and one page in window 101. **When** The user switches to Separate image connection before the attachment completes. **Then** The browser reaches an interactive state, retains the page at https://example.com, and still has exactly one target.
column11: Pending socket opening and pending native attachment are different cancellation boundaries. The donor does not leave a socket-open promise outstanding.

column5: **Given** A new tab is being created, and its first image is delayed. **When** Before the image arrives, the new tab's document navigates to https://destination.example.com/page. **Then** The previous page is not exposed. The address updates to the destination, a connecting message appears, and browser input remains disabled until the image arrives; after it arrives, the connecting message clears and input is enabled.
column6: **Given** An existing blank tab is available, and its first image is delayed. **When** The user selects it, and before the image arrives its document navigates to https://destination.example.com/page. **Then** The previous page is not exposed. The address updates to the destination, a connecting message appears, and browser input remains disabled until the image arrives; after it arrives, the connecting message clears and input is enabled.
column11: New tab creation and selecting an existing blank tab begin with different ownership histories before navigation. Both protect against displaying the previous page.

column5: **Given** The user has queued text input and starts copying it. **When** They blur the remote-browser input while the copy is queued, then enter fresh text. **Then** The copy is cancelled with an AbortError and no failure is reported. Fresh text is sent to the Example tab, and the input remains enabled.
column6: **Given** The user has started copying text while the copy is reading from the page. **When** They blur the remote-browser input before reading finishes, then enter fresh text. **Then** The copy is cancelled with an AbortError and no failure is reported. Fresh text is sent to the Example tab, and the input remains enabled.
column11: Queued copy and a copy already reading are different pending phases at blur. The donor does not exercise cancellation before reading begins.

column5: **Given** A chat contains a Markdown browser-authorization link with an absolute app URL and a callback prompt to continue the previous task; the request is valid and pending. **When** The user selects “Allow.” **Then** The request becomes allowed and disabled, and the app sends and displays the callback prompt only after authorization succeeds. The original chat message remains visible.
column6: **Given** A chat contains a browser-authorization link with an absolute app URL and a callback prompt to continue the previous task; the request is valid and pending. **When** The user selects “Allow.” **Then** The request becomes allowed and disabled, and the app sends and displays the callback prompt only after authorization succeeds. The original chat message remains visible.
column11: Markdown labeled link and bare URL use different parsing and rendering paths before the same approval and continuation outcome.

column5: **Given** The user is on the Okou home page. **When** The page loads. **Then** Compliance statuses appear below the capability cards and above the composer: SOC 2 Type II is In progress; CCPA / CPRA and GDPR are Compliant; HIPAA and ISO/IEC 27001 are Aligned.
column6: **Given** The user is in an empty conversation. **When** The conversation loads. **Then** Compliance statuses appear below the capability cards and above the composer: SOC 2 Type II is In progress; CCPA / CPRA and GDPR are Compliant; HIPAA and ISO/IEC 27001 are Aligned.
column11: Capability Home and the empty conversation are distinct surfaces. Compliance placement on one does not prove parity on the other.

column5: **Given** An artifact is open in the sidebar, and sharing data is available before ownership data. **When** The user waits for both reads to finish. **Then** Until ownership resolves, the content is visible but Download is hidden; once it resolves, Download, Share, and More actions appear.
column6: **Given** An artifact is open in the sidebar, and ownership data is available before sharing data. **When** The user waits for both reads to finish. **Then** Until sharing resolves, the content is visible but Download is hidden; once it resolves, Download, Share, and More actions appear.
column11: Sharing resolves before ownership here. The donor releases ownership first and does not cover the hidden-action state while ownership remains pending.

column5: **Given** An assistant message contains the absolute `https://app.okou.ai/artifacts/f000000000004000a000000000000941.png` reference. **When** The user opens the chat on the production host and opens the image preview. **Then** The thread image uses a thumbnail URL that preserves the reference, and the preview opens the resolved original URL.
column6: **Given** An assistant message contains the relative artifact reference `/artifacts/f000000000004000a000000000000941.png`. **When** The user opens the chat on the production host and opens the image preview. **Then** The thread image uses a thumbnail URL that preserves the reference, and the preview opens the resolved original URL.
column11: The absolute artifact URL exercises origin recognition. A relative path does not cover that normalization boundary.

column5: **Given** The chat has a Slack source and a related created chat, while the children response is pending. **When** The resource panel is opened before that response arrives, then the response completes. **Then** The panel shows a loading indicator without the Slack source initially; afterward it shows both the Slack source and related chat, with loading cleared.
column6: **Given** The chat has a Slack source and a related created chat, while the communications response is pending. **When** The resource panel is opened before that response arrives, then the response completes. **Then** The panel shows a loading indicator without the Slack source initially; afterward it shows both the Slack source and related chat, with loading cleared.
column11: Children first and communications first leave different external reads outstanding while the user waits for the joint section.

column5: **Given** The user is viewing the first of two chats, whose resources panel shows first.pdf. **When** The user navigates to the second chat while its artifacts are still loading, then opens its resources panel and waits for loading to finish. **Then** The new chat starts with the panel closed; it shows a loading status, not first.pdf, and after loading shows second.pdf without first.pdf.
column6: **Given** The user is viewing the first of two chats, whose resources panel shows first.pdf. **When** The user navigates to the second chat while its messages are still loading, then opens its resources panel and waits for loading to finish. **Then** The new chat starts with the panel closed; it shows a loading status, not first.pdf, and after loading shows second.pdf without first.pdf.
column11: The artifacts request is held here. The donor delays messages, so it cannot prove that stale resources stay hidden until artifacts arrive.

column5: **Given** The chat is ready and a new prompt has not yet been acknowledged by the run service. **When** The user sends “Summarize the launch risks.” **Then** The prompt immediately appears once in history with “Thinking...” and no queued-message row. After acceptance, Stop appears while thinking continues; after completion, the result appears, Send returns, and Stop disappears.
column6: **Given** The chat is ready and a newly sent prompt awaits service acknowledgement. **When** The user sends “Prepare the launch checklist,” then the prompt is queued, claimed by a run, and completed. **Then** Initially the prompt appears once with “Thinking...”. While queued, “Waiting in” and the queue control appear, Send remains available, and neither Thinking nor Stop appears. Once claimed, the queue control is replaced by Stop and Thinking; after completion, the result appears, Send returns, Thinking and Stop disappear, and the prompt remains in history once.
column11: The source tests direct acceptance with no queued row and uninterrupted Thinking. The donor explicitly transitions through Waiting before the Run claims the prompt.

column5: **Given** A chat thread contains only one assistant message, with no Run identity or associated Run events. **When** The user opens the thread. **Then** The message “Message delivered without a Run” is displayed.
column6: **Given** A chat thread contains a completed Run followed by an assistant message with no Run identity or associated Run events. **When** The user opens the thread. **Then** The message “Message delivered without a Run” is displayed after the Run.
column11: A thread with only a runless message and a runless delivery after a Run exercise different transcript context.

column5: **Given** The reader is in history at a narrow viewport, with a message anchored at the current reading position. **When** They open and close Automations, revealing the transcript. **Then** After the reveal, the anchored message returns to the same screen position with exactly one scroll adjustment.
column6: **Given** The reader has moved from the tail into history at a narrow viewport, with a message anchored at that live reading position. **When** They open and close Automations, revealing the transcript. **Then** After the reveal, the anchored message returns to the same screen position with exactly one scroll adjustment.
column11: The source starts in history without a prior tail transition. The donor covers a newly captured history offset after having been pinned to the tail.

column5: **Given** The reader is at the transcript tail at a narrow viewport. **When** They open and close Automations, revealing the transcript. **Then** After the reveal, the anchored message returns to the same screen position with exactly one scroll adjustment.
column6: **Given** The reader has moved from the tail into history at a narrow viewport, with a message anchored at that live reading position. **When** They open and close Automations, revealing the transcript. **Then** After the reveal, the anchored message returns to the same screen position with exactly one scroll adjustment.
column11: The source restores a tail anchor. The donor moves to a historical reading offset after tail and cannot observe tail restoration.

column5: **Given** A consent browser opens at /settings/discord?status=pending with a valid approval fragment, an opener, and an account that is not yet connected. **When** The consent browser verifies the account and the approval request succeeds. **Then** The fragment is cleared, the page says it is verifying the connection, and it does not close or show Open Discord while completion is pending.
column6: **Given** A consent browser opens at /works?discord=pending with a valid approval fragment, an opener, and an account that is not yet connected. **When** The consent browser verifies the account and the approval request succeeds. **Then** The fragment is cleared, the page says it is verifying the connection, and it does not close or show Open Discord while completion is pending.
column11: Current Discord settings and legacy Works callback routes must independently reach consent and preserve the current account while completion is pending.

column5: **Given** The Discord integration has two available workspaces, Design team and Operations, with Design team selected as the default. **When** The user selects Operations as the default workspace. **Then** The workspace choice remains disabled while refreshed status is pending. After refreshed status arrives, the choice is enabled and displays Operations.
column6: **Given** The default Discord direct-message workspace is Design team, and a save of Operations is pending while a status refresh succeeds. **When** The user selects Operations and a Discord status-change event triggers the refresh. **Then** The workspace selector remains disabled throughout the refresh and shows Design team; Design team is not offered as an option while disabled. After the save completes, the selector is enabled and shows Operations.
column11: This case saves successfully before the status refresh begins. The donor leaves save pending and injects an independent realtime refresh before completing it.

column5: **Given** A Tailscale network has one SSH connection and one VNC connection linked to it. **When** The user opens the network details page directly. **Then** The page shows both connection names in a read-only list with no links or buttons and no Add connection action.
column6: **Given** A Cloudflare Access network has one SSH connection and one VNC connection linked to it. **When** The user opens the network details page directly. **Then** The page shows both connection names in a read-only list with no links or buttons and no Add connection action.
column11: Tailscale and Cloudflare Access resolve linked references from distinct provider records. The common page outcome does not establish the other mapping.

column5: **Given** A member starts creating a Tailscale network and chooses to enter existing credentials. **When** The credential form opens. **Then** Only me is selected by default, the Organization members option is disabled, and the page explains that Engineering members can use the network while organization administrators create and manage organization networks.
column6: **Given** A member starts creating a Cloudflare Access network and chooses to enter existing credentials. **When** The credential form opens. **Then** Only me is selected by default, the Organization members option is disabled, and the page explains that Engineering members can use the network while organization administrators create and manage organization networks.
column11: Tailscale and Cloudflare Access creation have distinct provider inputs. Each member-facing path needs organization scope disabled.

column5: **Given** An administrator edits a personal Tailscale network that has a saved SSH connection reference. **When** They change its name to Shared office draft, select Organization members, and save while the sharing operation is pending. **Then** Saving proceeds without a confirmation dialog; after sharing completes, details show the edited name and organization scope, and the saved SSH connection reference remains intact.
column6: **Given** An administrator edits a personal Cloudflare Access network that has a saved SSH connection reference. **When** They change its name to Shared office draft, select Organization members, and save while the sharing operation is pending. **Then** Saving proceeds without a confirmation dialog; after sharing completes, details show the edited name and organization scope, and the saved SSH connection reference remains intact.
column11: Tailscale and Cloudflare promotion update distinct provider records and linked host references; the donor cannot prove the other provider update.

column5: **Given** An administrator has an existing personal Tailscale network and a personal Cloudflare Access network. **When** They create a Tailscale network named New team network, explicitly select Organization members, enter credentials, and save. **Then** The new network appears under Organization networks while the existing personal network remains unchanged in Personal networks.
column6: **Given** An administrator has an existing personal Tailscale network and a personal Cloudflare Access network. **When** They create a Cloudflare Access network named New team network, explicitly select Organization members, enter credentials, and save. **Then** The new network appears under Organization networks while the existing personal network remains unchanged in Personal networks.
column11: Tailscale and Cloudflare creation use different provider contracts to save organization scope while retaining personal networks.

column5: **Given** The sidebar is open on Nova’s chat, with read and unread conversations and the Research Agent pinned. **When** The user activates Nova and then Research Agent while holding Meta. **Then** The current URL and selected agent remain Nova’s chat. The unread conversation stays visible and the read conversation stays hidden.
column6: **Given** The sidebar is open on Nova’s chat, with read and unread conversations and the Research Agent pinned. **When** The user activates Nova and then Research Agent while holding Control. **Then** The current URL and selected agent remain Nova’s chat. The unread conversation stays visible and the read conversation stays hidden.
column11: Meta activating pinned links is a separate supported modifier condition from Control, even when both preserve the same selection.

column5: **Given** Slack confirms the user is connected and installed as an admin; the URL contains `status=connected`. **When** The user opens the Slack settings page and then focuses the window. **Then** Slack is launched once, the page shows “Slack is connected” and retains an “Open Slack” link, and focusing the window does not launch Slack again.
column6: **Given** Slack confirms the user is connected and installed as an admin; the URL has no query string. **When** The user opens the Slack settings page and then focuses the window. **Then** Slack is launched once, the page shows “Slack is connected” and retains an “Open Slack” link, and focusing the window does not launch Slack again.
column11: Slack's confirmed callback URL includes a status marker. Bare entry cannot prove the one-launch rule on a callback.

column5: **Given** A signed Telegram connection URL with prompt and repeated context parameters opens at /telegram/connect, and the account still needs setup. **When** The page loads. **Then** The setup page appears while the browser is on /settings/telegram with all query parameters preserved. An Open setup link opens /onboarding in a new tab, and Connect is not shown.
column6: **Given** A signed Telegram connection URL with prompt and repeated context parameters opens at /settings/telegram, and the account still needs setup. **When** The page loads. **Then** The setup page appears while the browser remains on /settings/telegram with all query parameters preserved. An Open setup link opens /onboarding in a new tab, and Connect is not shown.
column11: The legacy Telegram route must normalize to settings and preserve the signed query. The settings route already starts at the canonical path.

column5: **Given** A user opens /settings/telegram with the official bot selected, but Telegram login is not configured for the app. **When** The page loads. **Then** A Connection failed page explains that Telegram login could not be verified and advises contacting support. Back to settings links to Works, and Continue with Telegram is absent.
column6: **Given** A user opens /telegram/connect with the official bot selected, but Telegram login is not configured for the app. **When** The page loads. **Then** A Connection failed page explains that Telegram login could not be verified and advises contacting support. Back to settings links to Works, and Continue with Telegram is absent.
column11: The unavailable-configuration check covers a separately accepted Telegram entry route. Verify independent route-entry coverage before retiring either row.

column5: **Given** The onboarding prompt is “计算1加2，只回复数字。”. **When** The user continues to the first chat without choosing a format. **Then** The prompt is submitted unchanged; Document is not selected by default.
column6: **Given** The onboarding prompt asks what 1 + 2 is and explicitly requests only the number in reply. **When** The prompt loads and the user continues to the first chat. **Then** The prompt remains unchanged, Document is not selected by default, and the submitted chat prompt exactly matches the original prompt.
column11: Current response-format detection has a separate Chinese regex. The English reply-only case cannot exercise it or verify sending the Chinese text unchanged.

column5: **Given** An administrator who needs onboarding opens the retired invite URL with redeemCode=LAUNCH50. **When** The URL loads. **Then** The user is taken to the experience question, and the redeem code remains in the URL.
column6: **Given** A non-administrator who needs onboarding opens the retired invite URL with redeemCode=LAUNCH50. **When** The URL loads. **Then** The user is taken to the experience question, and the redeem code remains in the URL.
column11: The retired team-route command unconditionally redirects. With onboarding pending and only redeemCode present, the destination uses role for telemetry; both rows assert the same heading, route and preserved redeem code.

column5: **Given** The workflow instructions contain saved Markdown text. **When** The user focuses the editor, replaces its content, and undoes the edit. **Then** The original saved content returns and the unsaved-changes indicator disappears.
column6: **Given** The workflow Markdown file notes.md contains saved Markdown text. **When** The user focuses the editor, replaces its content, and undoes the edit. **Then** The original saved content returns and the unsaved-changes indicator disappears.
column11: Workflow Instructions and Markdown-file editors expose distinct backing content and undo histories. The Markdown donor cannot preserve undo for Instructions.

column5: **Given** The workflow instructions are saved, and an attempted update will initially fail with a conflict. **When** The user edits the instructions and saves, then retries after the conflict is no longer returned. **Then** After the failed save, the draft remains, the unsaved indicator remains, and Save is enabled. After the successful retry, the unsaved indicator clears and the submitted update contains the new instructions.
column6: **Given** The workflow Markdown file notes.md is saved, and an attempted update will initially fail with a conflict. **When** The user edits the file content and saves, then retries after the conflict is no longer returned. **Then** After the failed save, the draft remains, the unsaved indicator remains, and Save is enabled. After the successful retry, the unsaved indicator clears and the submitted update contains the new notes.md content.
column11: Instructions and Markdown file saves target different content; the donor does not cover preserving an Instructions draft after a rejected request.

column5: **Given** The workflow instructions are saved, and the user has made an unsaved edit. **When** They discard the edit and then try to undo it before making another edit. **Then** The saved instructions return, the unsaved indicator stays absent, and undo does not restore the discarded edit. A subsequent edit is shown as unsaved.
column6: **Given** The workflow Markdown file notes.md is saved, and the user has made an unsaved edit. **When** They discard the edit and then try to undo it before making another edit. **Then** The saved file content returns, the unsaved indicator stays absent, and undo does not restore the discarded edit. A subsequent edit is shown as unsaved.
column11: The Instructions editor and a file editor own different draft state. The donor cannot confirm Instructions undo history clears after discard.

column5: **Given** A user opens the info tab for a workflow that no longer exists. **When** The detail request cannot find the workflow. **Then** The page shows “Workflow not found.” and returns to Workflows, where Ops Playbook is listed.
column6: **Given** A user opens the instructions tab for a workflow that no longer exists. **When** The detail request cannot find the workflow. **Then** The page shows “Workflow not found.” and returns to Workflows, where Ops Playbook is listed.
column11: Workflow Info and Instructions are distinct detail routes. A missing Instructions route does not prove Info also redirects with the toast.

column5: **Given** An SSH access request is pending approval. **When** The user approves it, continuation fails with a service-unavailable response, and the user retries Continue task. **Then** The approved access remains in place while continuation is pending. The retry succeeds without another grant; two continuation attempts occur and only Revoke remains available.
column6: **Given** A VNC request can be approved, but continuing its task initially fails with a service error. **When** The user allows access, then retries the task continuation. **Then** The retry completes without granting access a second time; the card ends with only the revoke action available.
column11: SSH and VNC use their own grant and callback flows. A VNC retry does not exercise the SSH no-second-grant contract.

column5: **Given** A chat contains a forwarded link to an SSH request owned by a different chat. **When** The user opens the forwarded request card. **Then** The request is unavailable, and the user is told to ask for a new request.
column6: **Given** A VNC request linked in one chat belongs to a different chat thread. **When** The user opens the forwarded request card. **Then** The card says the request is unavailable and asks for a new request; it cannot be approved.
column11: Foreign-chat rejection must hold for SSH and VNC separately. One protocol request cannot prove the other's request binding.

column5: **Given** An SSH request requires the accompanying Cloudflare dns.write permission, and the requesting Run is initially blocked by that requirement. **When** The user opens the request page, then connector permission and Run state updates arrive. **Then** Approval is disabled while connector approval is required and the required permission is shown. If the Run is active, the page says to wait for it to finish; after the block clears, approval becomes available and succeeds.
column6: **Given** A VNC request is blocked by a required Cloudflare dns.write permission. **When** The connector permission changes to a requesting Run in progress, then the Run finishes and the user allows access. **Then** Allowing is disabled while either prerequisite remains, with the relevant explanation displayed. Once both prerequisites clear, allowing is enabled and access is approved.
column11: SSH and VNC approval flows depend on different connector requirements and request state. Each must become actionable when its own requirements clear.

column5: **Given** A GitHub account named octocat has two threads that will return to default inheritance if disconnected. **When** The user starts disconnecting it, the first attempt fails, and the user retries successfully. **Then** The confirmation explains that the Okou connection is removed, two threads return to default inheritance, and the provider account is not deleted. While the request is pending the disconnect button is disabled; on failure the dialog stays open with “Disconnect failed” and an enabled retry. The successful retry leaves no accounts, enables Add account, and closes the confirmation.
column6: **Given** An active personal subscription account is connected and disconnecting it initially fails. **When** The user confirms disconnect, receives a server failure, and retries the disconnect. **Then** During the request, the disconnect and cancel controls are disabled. After failure, “Disconnect failed” appears while the dialog and account remain, and disconnect can be retried. The successful retry closes the dialog, removes the account, and shows “Account disconnected.”
column11: GitHub connector disconnect restores inheritance for affected threads. The donor removes a Codex model provider account and does not check inheritance.

column5: **Given** A standalone computer authorization request has an online computer and is opened with a callback thread and the prompt “Continue.” **When** The user authorizes the computer. **Then** The computer is authorized exactly once and the button becomes disabled as “Authorized.” The “Continue” callback prompt is sent.
column6: **Given** The standalone Shell page has callback prompt “Continue” and a chat ID. **When** The user approves the request. **Then** Revoke becomes available, and “Continue” is sent to the chat.
column11: Computer Use and Desktop Shell approve distinct capabilities; the callback after one successful grant cannot cover the other.

column5: **Given** A standalone computer authorization request has an online computer and is opened without a callback thread or callback prompt. **When** The user authorizes the computer. **Then** The computer is authorized exactly once and the button becomes disabled as “Authorized.” No callback prompt is sent.
column6: **Given** The standalone Shell page has no callback prompt. **When** The user approves the request. **Then** Revoke becomes available, and no prompt is sent to the chat.
column11: Computer Use without callback and Shell without callback exercise different grants and confirmation states.

column5: **Given** A user opens the standalone Browser authorization page with a callback thread ID and the prompt “Continue.” **When** The user enables cloud browser for the thread. **Then** Authorization is granted once, and a follow-up chat prompt containing “Continue” is sent.
column6: **Given** The standalone Shell page has callback prompt “Continue” and a chat ID. **When** The user approves the request. **Then** Revoke becomes available, and “Continue” is sent to the chat.
column11: Browser enablement and Shell approval have different route and grant boundaries before continuation.

column5: **Given** A user opens the standalone Browser authorization page with a callback thread ID and the prompt “Continue.” **When** The user enables cloud browser for the thread. **Then** Authorization is granted once, and a follow-up chat prompt containing “Continue” is sent.
column6: **Given** A standalone computer authorization request has an online computer and is opened with a callback thread and the prompt “Continue.” **When** The user authorizes the computer. **Then** The computer is authorized exactly once and the button becomes disabled as “Authorized.” The “Continue” callback prompt is sent.
column11: Browser thread authorization and a Computer Use device grant are separate public entries, despite the shared Continue text.

column5: **Given** A user opens the standalone Browser authorization page with no callback thread or prompt parameters. **When** The user enables cloud browser for the thread. **Then** Authorization is granted once, and no follow-up chat prompt is sent.
column6: **Given** The standalone Shell page has no callback prompt. **When** The user approves the request. **Then** Revoke becomes available, and no prompt is sent to the chat.
column11: Browser no-callback and Shell no-callback must suppress continuation at their individual grant boundaries.

column5: **Given** A user opens the standalone Browser authorization page with no callback thread or prompt parameters. **When** The user enables cloud browser for the thread. **Then** Authorization is granted once, and no follow-up chat prompt is sent.
column6: **Given** A standalone computer authorization request has an online computer and is opened without a callback thread or callback prompt. **When** The user authorizes the computer. **Then** The computer is authorized exactly once and the button becomes disabled as “Authorized.” No callback prompt is sent.
column11: Browser thread and Computer Use device authorization must each suppress continuation when callback context is absent.

column5: **Given** An organization admin is viewing a directory containing the custom connector “First API.” **When** They start deleting it, close the pending deletion, open a new connector form, and enter “Second API draft.” The deletion then completes. **Then** The directory shows its empty-state message, while the new connector form remains open with “Second API draft.”
column6: **Given** The user is editing “First API” and has changed its name to “Saved first API” and its prefix to “http://api.acme.test/v1/”. **When** The user saves the edit, closes the edit dialog while the save is pending, and opens a new custom connector draft named “Second API draft.” The save then completes. **Then** The saved connector appears as “Saved first API,” and the new connector dialog remains open with “Second API draft” preserved.
column11: One races DELETE and one races UPDATE against a new draft. Different endpoint completions, list effects and success paths can close that draft.

column5: **Given** A pending SSH access request appears in a chat that owns the request. It identifies deploy@ssh.example.com:22 and states that access is limited to this host and chat. **When** The user opens Access details, allows access, and then revokes it. **Then** The details explain commands and file transfers and show the request reason. Access is allowed after one approval and can then be revoked.
column6: **Given** A chat contains a VNC access request for Work Mac at ssh.example.com:5900, with access limited to this chat. **When** The user opens access details, dismisses them, allows access, and then revokes it. **Then** The card describes viewing and controlling the desktop and shows the request reason. Allowing and revoking access each display the corresponding confirmation.
column11: SSH shows a remote user and VNC a desktop. Each inline card grants its specific request only to the current chat.
